_comment: Every command below sources ONE interpreter probe, `hooks/probe-python.sh`,
which leaves a usable Python 3.8+ in $PYEXE or refuses and exits 1. That
script carries the full rationale: why it RUNS each candidate instead of
trusting `command -v`, why the check is a version rather than liveness, why
the three names are not sufficient on their own, and why refusal is
non-zero. Read it before changing anything here.
The probe used to be a ~500-char one-liner inlined into all five commands,
plus a `_pyexe` reference copy in this file. JSON has no substitution, so
the copies were held equal only by a test, and they had drifted from the
reference once already. Both the duplication and `_pyexe` are gone; the
script is the single source, and `test_every_wiring_sources_the_shared_probe`
pins that every command still reaches it.
The `||` clause covers the one case sourcing adds: a MISSING probe file.
bash prints its own error and then CONTINUES, which would run the hook with
$PYEXE empty; sh exits 1 on its own and never reaches the clause. Verified
on both. An `exit` inside a probe that IS present exits this shell
immediately, so the clause cannot mask a refusal.

hooks.command: . "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/probe-python.sh" || { echo "cla: interpreter probe missing at ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/probe-python.sh — guard hooks are NOT running" >&2; exit 1; }; "$PYEXE" "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/dispatch-edit-write-pretooluse.py"

. "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/probe-python.sh" || { echo "cla: interpreter probe missing at ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/probe-python.sh — guard hooks are NOT running" >&2; exit 1; }; "$PYEXE" "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/dispatch-bash-pretooluse.py"
